rule_or_pattern: Drop lines flagged C:repeated_word, C:cpp_vs_book_out or C:cph_out_of_range (fragmented/overlapping line boxes in the small-print etymology blocks: label is a partial, doubled or different reading of a crop that spans parts of 2-3 print lines). Also drop labels matching \b(\S+\.?) \1\b (immediately repeated token).
notes: Normal-size dictionary lines read correctly (3, 5-19, 23, 26, 28, 31, 34, 38); the genre (abbreviated citations, numbers, hyphenated roots) explains the B/C outliers. The small-print blocks on spread pages are segmented badly by Google (page.jpg shows overlapping boxes): crops 1, 2, 20, 32, 40 span several print lines and the label is only part of it or a different line, and 24, 25, 27, 29, 30, 35, 37 carry doubled readings (e.g. 'Αριστ. Αριστ.', 'προσεκτικῶς, προσεκτικῶς', 'ὑπερσ. ὑπερσ. γ. πλ. ἐπ. ἐπ.'). Roughly 10-15% of lines, concentrated in those flags.
